title: Electrophysiological analysis of Gamma-Hydroxybutyrate-induced sleep in intensive care patients: A Pilot Double-Blind Randomized Controlled Trial
official: Electrophysiological analysis of Gamma-Hydroxybutyrate-induced sleep in intensive care patients: A Pilot Double-Blind Randomized Controlled Trial.(GAMMA-SLEEP)
summary: Main objective: The primary objective of this pilot study is to show that the intravenous administration of GHB improves the duration (in minutes) of deep slow-wave sleep (N3 stage) in critically ill adult patients compared to a placebo
conditions: The study population includes adult ICU patients with a hospitalization of more than 48 hours. We have chosen to include patients with or without mechanical ventilation, as sleep disorders affect all ICU patients after 48 hours.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Aged 18 years or older
2. Hospitalized in the ICU for more than 48 hours
3. Informed consent obtained from the patient
Exclusion criteria:
1. Unstable patient
2. Recent head trauma or neurological injury
3. Severe hypertension: SBP > 180 mmHg despite antihypertensive treatment
4. Hypokalemia < 3.5 mmol/L despite potassium supplementation
5. Patients with known or suspected succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase (SSADH) deficiency, given the risk of GHB accumulation due to impaired endogenous metabolism
6. Patients receiving opioids at inclusion for non-mechanically ventilated patient
7. Patients presenting with hypernatraemia (sodium > 145 mmol/L) or hyperchloraemia (chloride > 110 mmol/L) at inclusion
8. Patients with hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh B or C)
9. Cardiac conduction disorder
10. Obstructive sleep apnea syndrome
11. Sodium restriction: Salt intake < 3g/24h
12. Lack of social security or on AME (state medical aid)
13. Deep sedation defined by a RASS score < -2
14. Presence of mental confusion: Positive CAM-ICU
15. Moribund patient or high likelihood of death within 48 hours
16. Legal protection: guardianship, curatorship, or judicial protection
17. Patients receiving barbiturates at inclusion
18. Participation in another interventional clinical trial related to the management of sleep disorders, delirium, or sedation in the ICU.
19. Known allergy to Gamma-Hydroxybutyrate or any of the exipients
20. Technical impossibility of performing polysomnography
21. Positive pregnancy test for women of childbearing age or breastfeeding
22. Patient who has already received the study treatment
23. History of chronic alcoholism
24. Uncontrolled epilepsy despite appropriate antiepileptic treatment
